# Data card

**All wells, reports and events in this repository are synthetic.** They are generated by `ai_service/scripts/generate_synthetic.py` and `make_reports.py` with a fixed seed (42 and 7), are not Oil India data, and must not be presented as real operational records.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Wells | 61 (60 historical + the active demo well WELL-A-102), around a made-up field location |
| Drilling rows | 23,431 (1,500 m to TD every 5 m); plus a 200-row replay stream for WELL-A-102 |
| Events (ground truth) | 82: 36 mud_loss, 33 torque_spike, 10 stuck_pipe, 3 kick |
| Reports | 30 PDFs (22 text, 8 scanned image-only), 222 pages; 25 reports contain events, 5 do not |
| Wells within 10 km of WELL-A-102 | 17 |
| Extracted entities | 1,213 across 30 documents |

## Planted patterns (what the system is expected to rediscover)

Mud loss around 2840 m in Formation X; stuck pipe around 3300 m in Formation Y (mostly directional wells); torque spikes around 2100 m in Formation C; occasional kicks around 3450 m. Zone depths shift with location to imitate formation dip. Each report states events in several phrasings and repeats them on a "lessons learned" page, so extraction has to deduplicate.

## What the numbers mean

Anything measured against this data (extraction F1, retrieval recall, risk back-test) shows that the pipeline recovers patterns that were planted. It is **not** accuracy on real drilling data.

The reported metrics below are therefore evaluation results on the supplied synthetic/template dataset and should not be interpreted as expected production performance on real drilling operations.

## Models used

Embeddings: `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (local). Extraction and assistant: `Gemini 3.8 Flash` (`gemini-3.8-flash`). Free-tier prompts may be retained by the provider: use synthetic or authorised data only.

## Additional evaluation

The risk engine was evaluated with controlled scenarios:

- Normal drilling near 2790 m: historical mud-loss risk detected.
- Approaching the risk zone near 2820 m: historical/high risk detected.
- Live anomaly near 2850 m: risk escalated to critical, score 93.
- Unrelated depth near 1000 m: no alert.

At 2850 m, the full risk score was 93. Removing individual scoring signals reduced the score to 68 without depth overlap, 73 without formation, 82 without similar-well evidence, 73 without same-event evidence, 78 without anomaly evidence, and 91 without proximity.

## Testing

The final core test suite passed:

- `17 passed` — offline, entity, and core tests.
- Targeted offline/entity tests: `14 passed`.

## AI/ML scope

The current production/demo risk alerts are generated by the evidence/rule-based risk engine combined with live anomaly detection.

An additional experimental ML package is maintained separately. It contains supervised event-risk modelling, severity modelling, SHAP/LIME explanations, drift monitoring, and an optional ML serving endpoint. These experimental components must not be treated as replacements for the core alert engine unless separately validated.

## Limitations

- The entire dataset is synthetic/template data.
- Results demonstrate recovery of planted patterns rather than real-world predictive accuracy.
- The event ground truth contains 82 events, while the extraction evaluation uses a separate 40-event evaluation set.
- Risk backtesting uses planted historical events and simulated drilling data.
- The experimental ML package has separate validation requirements and should be reported independently from the core rule/evidence-based system.
